name: Warmers
label: Dischord
lede: The kid on the cover of the first Minor Threat EP grew up, picked up a guitar, and built a trio around the space between the notes.

eras.title: Three people and a lot of air
eras.text: Alec MacKaye had sung in three DC bands since he was a teenager: the Untouchables, Faith and Ignition. This time he played guitar too, and went looking for a rhythm section that knew when not to play.

years.h: Alec MacKaye joins Amy Farina and Juan Luis Carrera
years.p: [[Alec MacKaye|bb05a948-ea44-4c9b-9d19-2a48f757ca22]], of [[Untouchables|16d88df0-a2a9-4b3b-87ff-84e90e312d40]], [[Faith|f735a867-9a16-451f-8f83-669ed42e2574]] and [[Ignition|3cb2b7d6-1f0b-4ac5-b67f-52132f3d3b61]], teams up with drummer [[Amy Farina|30d1b9a6-4156-49ec-84ba-65c3f5ebbf69]] and bassist Juan Luis Carrera after seeing them play. Dischord dates the Warmers from July 1994.
years.xp:
Farina and Carrera had already made a 7" together before Alec MacKaye came in. He was a known face long before the Warmers: the kid slumped on the cover of [[Minor Threat|09037f07-42bc-46ac-a1ee-37f834451fee]]'s first EP, and on [[The Teen Idles|84e8d8bf-da21-4488-89e5-50a4c12ff4fa]]' Minor Disturbance, is Alec.

Dischord's bio sums up the idea in one line: the Warmers wanted open space, with silence treated as an instrument on equal footing with bass, guitar, drums and voice.

years.p: The Warmers' first single has two songs, Thin Air and Occupation: Fish, the latter a tribute to baseball player Roberto Clemente. It is long out of print.

eras.title: Silence as an instrument
eras.text: The Warmers made one album, Warmers, cut at Inner Ear with Ian MacKaye, and spent a lot of time in a van. Amy Farina's drumming, all held breath and late arrivals, became the thing people talked about.

years.p: The Warmers' only album: fourteen songs recorded at Inner Ear, produced by [[Ian MacKaye|c12f644b-1066-4ead-b0dd-d0c380f5cca2]] and the band. Snake Charmer, The Lowdown and Poked It With a Stick show the method: lean, clipped, and full of gaps.
years.xp:
Critics singled out the minimalism and, above all, Amy Farina's drums. Alec MacKaye has described what floored him about Farina: she holds off where a drummer is supposed to hit, then comes in late.

The LP and CD are out of print; the songs survive as a Dischord digital release.

years.h: The Warmers tour with Sonic Youth and Blonde Redhead
years.p: Dischord's bio says the Warmers toured the US extensively, sharing bills with [[Sonic Youth|5cbef01b-cc35-4f52-af7b-d0df0c4f61b9]] and [[Blonde Redhead|6821bf3f-5d5b-4b0f-8fa4-79d2ab2d9219]].

years.h: The Warmers' only European show: a festival in Sicily
years.p: The Warmers' only European date is a festival in Sicily.
Three and a half years after it started, the Warmers stop. Dischord dates the band's run July 1994 to December 1997.

eras.title: Wanted: more
eras.text: The Warmers came back only on record: once on Dischord's 20 Years of Dischord box and once with their shelved last session, Wanted: More. The members kept going in other bands.

years.h: The Warmers on 20 Years of Dischord
years.p: The Warmers' Poked It With a Stick makes Dischord's anniversary box set, Dischord No. 125.

years.h: Wanted: More, the Warmers' shelved last session
years.p: Six songs recorded at Pirate House in December 1996 sat on a shelf for eight years. Dischord released them in 2004 as No. 144.
years.xp: Alec MacKaye, the band and [[Don Zientara|a495882b-4585-4295-9269-e30c63f279fe]] mixed the session. It includes Red Light Runner, Totally Free and Berretta USA.

years.h: Where the Warmers went: The Evens, Coriky, Hammered Hulls
years.p: Amy Farina, who married Alec's brother Ian MacKaye, plays with him in [[The Evens|3a3b3e5d-2d28-4108-875e-30686d2710e8]] and later [[Coriky|d471b090-3866-4cf3-b8a0-476e11f30a58]]. Alec MacKaye sings in [[Hammered Hulls|64368968-d520-49ea-a248-9ccc29e1467f]] and worked as chief preparator at the Phillips Collection in Washington.

sources.title: The Collapsar: No One Like Me, Amy Farina and the Warmers
